text: While you wait, put one hand on your heart and the other on your belly, and say to yourself: "This feeling is allowed to move through. I can love the part of me that feels it."
reader: someone alone in the night, mid-trip and scared, who has just sent a message to a calm person and is waiting

sentences.s: While you wait, put one hand on your heart and the other on your belly, and say to yourself: "This feeling is allowed to move through.
sentences.payoff: they have something to do with their hands and words while they wait: a hand on the heart and one on the belly, and a line that lets the feeling pass
sentences.follows: it fills the wait after the message the line before has them send

sentences.s: I can love the part of me that feels it."
sentences.payoff: they turn toward the frightened part of themselves with love instead of fighting it, the guide's method for fear, when nobody is there to bring it
sentences.follows: the second line of the same self-talk
sentences.link: none: it is the next line of the same quoted self-talk, so it needs no words tying it to the one before

placement: Alone at 3 a.m., right after "Send the human-anchor script." and before the movement lines; "While you wait" points to the reply to that message

opens.first_sentence: While you wait, put one hand on your heart and the other on your belly, and say to yourself: "This feeling is allowed to move through.
opens.why_reading: it tells someone alone and waiting what they can do for themselves right now, so they read on

same_point: none: read the section from its heading to the next for these points; it says the lamp, the keys, the message and movement, and nothing about what to do with the feeling itself. For the Person Helping has the same self-talk for the helper (this one is for someone alone)

needed.reader: a fresh Haiku agent given tools/humanization/needed_read_brief.md with the paragraph, its heading and what it is for (NEEDED-READ.raw.md beside this receipt, item 1)

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first, in each sentence and each paragraph; a study after the question it answers; a term explained where it is first used, never in a sentence after it)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine) Is every term a high-school graduate wouldn't know (enterocytes, BPC-157) explained once, where it is first used, and common ones (a vitamin) left alone? Is each mechanism explained by what it does in the reader's experience (dopamine "for motivation (by showing us what is important to pay attention to)"; DeltaFosB "preventing that learning from really clicking"), not by where it sits or what it looks like ("a chemical blanket", "the slower one underneath")? (E375)
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
question_text.Q9: Is anything compressed? (one step a sentence, the small words that carry the relation, no space before mg)
